# Adaptive Layouts

<!-- Generated by generate-swiftui-skill.py; edit the library sources. -->

Category: Layout

Reduce the available width to compare a rigid horizontal row with the same content arranged by the first layout candidate that fits.

- Before: Horizontal content overflows
- After: Layout adapts to available width

APIs: `ViewThatFits`, `HStack`, `VStack`

## Complete improved example

Adapt the behavior to the app; demonstration controls and values are illustrative.

```swift
import SwiftUI

// iOS 17+. Present FlexibleDoExample() in your app.
struct FlexibleDoExample: View {
    @State private var width: CGFloat = 160
    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 20) {
            FlexibleDoContent(availableWidth: width)
                .frame(maxWidth: 320, minHeight: 180)
            Button("Change width") { width = width > 200 ? 130 : 270 }
            Slider(value: $width, in: 130...280) { Text("Available width") }
            Button("Reset") { width = 160 }
        }
        .padding()
    }
}

struct FlexibleDoContent: View {
    var availableWidth: CGFloat = 160

    var body: some View {
        // excerpt:start
        ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal) {
            HStack { labels }
            VStack(alignment: .leading) { labels }
        }
        .frame(width: availableWidth, alignment: .leading)
        .border(.separator)
        // excerpt:end
    }

    @ViewBuilder private var labels: some View {
        Label("Delivery", systemImage: "shippingbox")
        Text("Tomorrow morning")
    }

}
```
